top.description: By Olayinka Latona The Fountain of Life Church today held its Sunday service despite reports of a court injunction against Pastor Jimmy Odukoya. Addressing the crowded congregation, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya said he had not received any court injunction as reported, and stressed his unwavering love for the church. Members were said to have chanted “We love you” during the service. Bishop Mike Okonkwo of The Redeemed Evangelical Ministry, one of the spiritual fathers to the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, ministered on the theme “The Glory of The Church.” He charged members and ministers of the church to diligently keep the founder’s legacy and remain steadfast in Christ, reminding them of the advice he gave when the church founder died. “The responsibility fell on us to talk to… The only honour we can do for the sacrifice, the process, pains and everything that the man of God who is highly celebrated in this country is that his legacy must continue,” Bishop Okonkwo said. “And I told you that day that Fountain will never die. No matter the trial or temptation, this is a work that is solidly laid. The price has been paid; lives have been lost. There is no power of hell that would destroy this work. It will go from glory to glory.” Acknowledging recent online attacks, he said: “For the past one or two weeks, we have been literally battered on social media. Phone calls from far and near: ‘Bishop Mike, where are you?’ You can’t separate me from Fountain; it’s not possible, because it’s a covenant established by God Himself. top.description: Quarterback Brock Purdy and the 49ers offense have faced four defenses in the bottom six of the NFL this season - the Falcons, Cowboys, Cardinals and Raiders - possibly skewing their effectiveness. (Tony Gutierrez/Associated Press) The San Francisco 49ers have already delivered some big wins - the opener in Australia against the Rams and beating the Seahawks in Seattle among them - but suddenly their game in Mexico City against a really good Minnesota Vikings team might be their biggest test yet. Before the two teams tangle, we asked columnist Ann Killion and reporters Eric Branch and Harrison Rich for their answers to some key questions about the matchup. Have mounting injuries already ended the prime of Nick Bosa 's career? Is this his new normal in terms of production? Harrison Rich: Bosa has not looked like his old self since returning two weeks ago from a calf injury. He didn't look like himself earlier in the season, either, when he was dealing with knee tendinitis coming off his second torn right ACL. The 29-year-old defensive end hasn't recorded a sack in four games this season, his longest NFL drought. He pointed to two factors Wednesday for his struggles: He's still learning some of the quirks of defensive coordinator Raheem Morris' scheme, and he's still knocking off some rust. Bosa said he took "for granted" some of the things he used to be able to do automatically. Sunday's game, expected to have playoff-like intensity, will tell us a lot about the heights Bosa is still capable of reaching. Ann Killion: It's probably safe to say that Bosa will never again be the dominant force that he was in 2021 and 2022. Four years later, he's 29 and has a history of serious knee injuries. The fact that he thought, as he said this week, that he could "coast" and do the things he used to do "automatically" is an indication of just how hard it is for elite athletes to stay at that level, not only physically but mentally. Bosa's honest assessment this week means he will be even more in the spotlight in Sunday's game, where Minnesota's pass rush is expected to be the star. Eric Branch: It's a question Bosa might be asking himself. It was notable this week that Bosa admitted he was surprised he hasn't been able to return from last year's torn ACL and "automatically" perform at his All-Pro level. His extensive medical file includes three torn ACLs, two on the right knee he injured in 2025. Still, Bosa has shown some dominant flashes, such as when he hit Dak Prescott's arm in mid-throw last Sunday in Dallas after bullying right tackle Terence Steele with a bull rush. Also, Bosa has played in just four games this season, which qualifies as a small sample size. Verdict: It's premature to bury Bosa. top.title: Randy Flores brings a former player's perspective to Houston Astros GM job - and knows its limits
top.description: From player to scout to Astros GM, Randy Flores says firsthand experience helps him understand players - if he stays open to other perspectives. (Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle) In his first year as St. Louis Cardinals scouting director , Randy Flores was watching a pitcher who threw a four-seam fastball and a curveball. The mix can be the backbone of a north-south pitching profile. But to Flores, a former major-league reliever, it looked suboptimal. "I'm like, ‘No, no, no - you sink it and slide it,'" said Flores, reciting an approach he gleaned from former Cardinals pitching coach Dave Duncan. As a slight left-hander who did not throw especially hard, Flores carved out a playing career that lasted parts of eight major-league seasons. So, his methods had merit. But as an executive now, he recalls the scouting anecdote as something of a cautionary tale. "Being a former player, if you're anchored too much to, ‘This is how it was done when I was playing,' it's the wrong thing," Flores said. Exploring other perspectives and means and finding a balance has been part of Flores' evolution as an executive, one that led to his hiring this month as general manager of the Houston Astros . It is also an arc to which only a handful of the majors' current highest-ranking baseball executives can relate. Of the current presidents of baseball operations, Jerry Dipoto (Mariners), Chris Young (Rangers), Craig Breslow (Red Sox) and Buster Posey (Giants) played in the majors. So did general managers Chris Getz (White Sox) and Flores, whom the Astros hired after 11-plus seasons in St. Louis' front office. That many top executives did not play in the majors, or at all professionally, illustrates how it is far from required. It might even invite the question of how such experience informs former players' approach to the role, if at all, as Flores settles into running a baseball operations department for the first time. "You probably have more empathy … for what a player goes through, from the moment they sign their first professional contract to when they get to the big leagues," Dipoto said at last week's GM meetings in Las Vegas. Dipoto and Breslow were relievers in the majors, like Flores. Dipoto posited that background could help "to understand the life of the guy who (is) not always the most thought-of player on the roster." "Outside of that, I think it's just business as usual," Dipoto said. "We each went through our own, I guess, apprenticeship (after playing). "You take the lessons you learn and apply them, just like any other general manager does when they get their first job. We just maybe have that slight - I don't even want to call it an advantage - that slight difference in that we have lived life in these players' shoes and probably as a result have a little bit more empathy rather than just frustration. top.description: Liverpool remain unsure over Virgil van Dijk contract decision Virgil van Dijk contract latest as Liverpool weigh renewal and AC Milan interest Liverpool are facing a significant call on the future of Virgil van Dijk, with fresh reporting from Sport Italia indicating that the club remain hesitant over the defender’s preferred contract terms. Van Dijk, now 35, remains one of the defining figures of this Liverpool side. Even through major change, including the end of the Arne Slot era and the arrival of Andoni Iraola, his place in the team has carried real weight. His level, leadership and authority have kept him central to Liverpool’s defensive structure, while younger players around him continue to develop. The issue is not whether Van Dijk still contributes. By all accounts, he does. The issue is what Liverpool are prepared to commit to next, and on what financial and sporting terms. Sport Italia report outlines key Virgil van Dijk dilemma The update from Italy points to a familiar modern stand-off between club caution and player expectation. Sport Italia state, “Gerry Cardinale is following the Reds captain’s situation and dreams of a big signing this summer. The sticking point is a renewal: the Dutchman is asking for a two-year contract, while Liverpool still seem unconvinced.” That immediately places AC Milan into the conversation, albeit at a watching distance for now. The same report adds, “Virgil van Dijk’s future could become one of the most interesting situations of the upcoming summer transfer window. AC Milan is in the background, with Gerry Cardinale eyeing the possibility of bringing one of the most authoritative defenders in the international scene to San Siro.” There is still an important caveat. Liverpool hold the contract, and the club’s decision remains the key factor. As Sport Italia put it, “But before imagining the Dutch centre-back in a Rossoneri shirt, Liverpool must be taken into account.” That is where the matter sharpens. “This is precisely where the crux of the matter lies: Van Dijk wants a two-year extension, while Liverpool do not appear willing, at least for now, to fully grant his request.” Photo: IMAGO Liverpool contract policy under focus again This feels less about emotion and more about policy. Van Dijk is Liverpool’s highest-paid player, and by the start of next season he will be 36. Clubs at the elite end have to judge not only present performance, but the durability of that performance over the life of a deal. top.description: Varsity matriculates 2,442 students for 2026/2027 session By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — Afe Babalola University, Ado-Ekiti (ABUAD), has warned newly admitted students against cultism, cybercrime, substance abuse and other social vices capable of undermining their education and future. The university also cautioned the students against examination malpractice, bullying and the irresponsible use of artificial intelligence, urging them to uphold discipline, integrity and academic excellence. The Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Smaranda Olarinde, gave the warning at the institution’s 18th matriculation ceremony held over the weekend, where 2,442 students were formally admitted for the 2026/2027 academic session. Addressing the students, the vice-chancellor described their admission as an opportunity that required discipline, responsibility and commitment to academic excellence. She urged them to be mindful of their associations, noting that their choice of friends could influence their habits, reputation, academic performance and future. According to her, university education goes beyond obtaining certificates to include character formation, emotional maturity, leadership development and the acquisition of values needed to contribute meaningfully to society. Olarinde urged the students to uphold the university’s philosophy of Labour, Service and Integrity, stressing that hard work, selfless service and honesty should guide their academic and professional pursuits. top.title: England won't get carried away by All Blacks win
top.description: [BBC] In his latest BBC Sport column, England World Cup winner Matt Dawson reflects on Steve Borthwick's side's record win over New Zealand and previews the final round of Nations Championship fixtures. If England had produced that performance two years ago against New Zealand, there would have been a lap of honour and wild celebrations. Saturday felt like business. Job done, move on. And that is how it should be. It was a record victory for a northern hemisphere side against the All Blacks, yet at full-time you would hardly have known it. Even the post-match messaging from their leaders - Maro Itoje, Ellis Genge and Steve Borthwick - was that this performance had always been in them and that nobody was surprised. However, they will want to back it up. A tired but hurting New Zealand side will arrive at Allianz Stadium next Saturday looking for revenge. England beat the All Blacks in back-to-back Tests in 2002 and 2003. Matching that achievement on Saturday was a significant statement. Three consecutive wins over New Zealand, followed by a third-place finish, would leave England in a strong position heading into 2027, when the Rugby World Cup takes place in Australia. Lose, though, and it will be a waste of some great momentum. We have had many a false dawn with Borthwick's England, but something feels different this time. For me, that comes down to the players taking responsibility. Many of us ex-pros called for it during the Six Nations, and finally we are seeing the players take the lead on the style of rugby they want to play. It is an exciting, free-flowing brand of attacking rugby that mirrors what they are used to playing in the Prem. England's backs can compete with the very best and they tore through New Zealand on multiple occasions. Credit also has to go to Borthwick for allowing the players to take control. That, in itself, shows how he is learning and evolving as a head coach. Once players start getting 40, 50, 60 or 70 caps, they know more about certain aspects of the game than the coach because they are the ones out there experiencing it. If the environment does not allow players to turn around and say 'this isn't going to work', then it is never going to work. The reports before the Australia game suggested honest conversations took place, with the players wanting a greater say in how the team operates. The Six Nations was probably a big turning point. The change in mood and the feel-good factor are clear in the way England are carrying themselves. They now feel in control and, crucially, have a genuine sense of ownership in shaping the team and how it plays. top.description: Chelsea boss Bompastor calls for better balance after draw at Liverpool Chelsea head coach Sonia Bompastor said that her her side need more balance between attack and defence after they drew 0-0 at Liverpool on Saturday afternoon. The Blues had chances to win the game, but they were unable to take full advantage as they dropped points in the title race. Speaking to the media after the match, Bompastor said that her side must have greater balance between defence and attack. “I’m really happy with a lot of things we are doing right now,” Bompastor said. “When you have ambitions, when you want to win titles, you need to make sure to find the right balance between being strong defensively, but also, being able to score goals. “I would like to have a better balance in terms of being able to score more.” Bompastor left it late to make attacking changes. Aggie Beever-Jones was not introduced until the 83rd minute. The Blues boss defended her decisions in the game. She said “I think all my decisions are based on performances. I think even if we were not able to score a goal in this game, what I was seeing on the pitch was good enough for me to still be confident. top.title: Porto rally around defender that was left in tears by horror own goal
top.description: Porto have rallied around Francisco Moura after the player scored a horror own goal in his side’s Portuguese Cup tie on Friday, which reduced him to tears. The 27-year-old defender passed the ball into his own net in the 57th minute of the fourth-round tie against third-division side Paredes, inexplicably kicking it into the bottom left corner after a save by his goalkeeper. Moura dropped straight to the ground with his hands over his face, covering his head with his jersey as he started crying. He then signalled to the bench that he wanted to be substituted. Moura, who received support from both sets of players following the blunder, was not immediately substituted and later came off in the 70th minute. top.title: Manchester City's torrid winless run in the Premier League extended to four games on Saturday afternoon as yet another lacklustre display from Enzo Maresca's men saw the Blues draw 1-1 with Fulham at the Etihad Stadium.
top.description: Manchester City's torrid winless run in the Premier League extended to four games on Saturday afternoon as yet another lacklustre display from Enzo Maresca's men saw the Blues draw 1-1 with Fulham at the Etihad Stadium. How does Enzo Maresca fix Manchester City's defence? A City performace that was, for large parts, void of intensity and creativity, saw the Blues fail to beat Fulham at the Etihad Stadium for the first time in 15 years, dating back to February 2011 under Roberto Mancini. There was hope that, after the international break, those of a sky-blue persuasion would be galvanised to right the wrongs of their recent shortcomings, having suffered three consecutive league defeats; unfortunately, however, it was more of the slothful same. In the opening exchanges, Maresca's men struggled to ride the storm of Fulham 's intensity but did conjure some somewhat presentable chances early on, with Erling Haaland seeing his effort thwarted by David Affengruber whilst a deflection steered Nico O'Reilly's shot narrowly wide. However, with just 16 minutes on the clock, Manchester City 's defensive frailties reared their ugly head once again as the Cottagers drew first blood in the tie through Rodrigo Muniz, who latched on to a superb pass from former Blue Oscar Bobb and hammered past Gianluigi Donnarumma to give the visitors the lead. Just eight minutes later, the home side thought they had restored parity after an excellent cross from Iliman Ndiaye found Haaland, and the 26-year-old, after squandering the initial chance, seized upon a goalkeeping mishap by Bernd Leno, prodding home after the German appeared to spill the ball. But referee Thomas Bramall, controversially brought the celebrations to an abrupt halt, having adjudged that the former Arsenal shot-stopper had two hands on the ball at the time of the Norwegian's follow-up, resulting in a foul and disallowed goal. Subsequently, a defensive blunder from O'Reilly nearly proved calamitous as the Englishman allowed Bobb to snatch possession inside the Manchester City area, but Donnarumma was on hand to spare his teammate's blushes and deny the Fulham number 14. After a dismal first 45 which saw the halftime whistle met with jeers from the Etihad Stadium crowd, Maresca was in dire need of an injection of impetus into his side, and 12 minutes after the restart, Elliott Anderson obliged, producing a sumptuous volley which nestled into the back of the Fulham net and hauled the hosts level. Whilst the goal certainly did breathe some life into the home side, City were still by no means at their scintillating best in the second period, with the lack of ideas and desire remaining a glaringly obvious issue. In truth, Fulham looked more likely to walk away with three points, but Donnarumma, whose shot-stopping was much improved, remained resolute, preventing both Muniz and Calvin Bassey from deciding the tie late on. nigeria.title: NELFUND considers increase in N20,000 monthly student upkeep
nigeria.description: By Joseph Erunke Millions of Nigerian students benefiting from the Federal Government’s student loan scheme may soon receive higher monthly upkeep allowances as the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND, considers a review of the current N20,000 payment amid mounting pressure from rising living costs. The possibility of an increase emerged as NELFUND acknowledged that the existing allowance might require adjustment to better reflect the financial realities facing students struggling to meet the costs of feeding, transportation, accommodation and other basic necessities while pursuing their education. The fund’s Managing Director, Akintunde Sawyer, disclosed this during an interview on Beyond the Headlines,a TVC news programme, where he said the monthly upkeep payment was under constant review. Although he did not announce a new figure or a timeline for implementation, Sawyer signalled that an adjustment was being considered, raising expectations among students who have repeatedly complained that the current ₦20,000 monthly allowance is inadequate to survive on in the face of escalating prices. “Are we considering it? Yes, of course. It’s under constant review,” he said. The indication of a possible increase comes against the backdrop of growing concerns over the purchasing power of students, many of whom depend on the NELFUND intervention to cushion the financial burden of higher education. nigeria.title: Nigerian sentenced to 24 months in US prison over COVID-19 relief fraud
nigeria.description: A Nigerian man, Chukwuebuka Arinze, has been sentenced to two years in prison in the United States for using another person’s identity to fraudulently apply for COVID-19 relief funds. Arinze, 38, was convicted of aggravated identity theft after using a farmer’s Social Security number to submit an application under the US government’s Coronavirus Food Assistance Program. He was sentenced on October 30, 2026, by US District Judge Robert Rossiter Jr. at a federal court in Omaha, Nebraska, according to the US Attorney’s Office for the District of Nebraska. The Nigerian will also serve one year of supervised release after his imprisonment and face deportation from the United States, the statement said. Prosecutors said Arinze, who was living outside the US at the time, sent an email to the Farm Service Agency office in Wayne, Nebraska, on September 28, 2020, seeking financial assistance under the programme. The email, titled “CFAP Forms,” contained an application for the second phase of the Coronavirus Food Assistance Program, known as CFAP2, alongside an Automated Clearing House payment form. Both documents were submitted in the name of a dairy farmer identified in court records as Victim 1 and contained the farmer’s Social Security number. The US authorities said Arinze knowingly used the identification number belonging to the farmer without authorisation to validate the application. He was later brought to the United States to face prosecution over the offence. The Coronavirus Food Assistance Program was established by the US Department of Agriculture during the COVID-19 pandemic to support agricultural producers affected by declining sales and rising marketing costs. The initiative was administered through the department’s Farm Service Agency and Agricultural Marketing Service. Its first phase ran from May 26 to September 11, 2020, while the second phase, CFAP2, opened from September 21 to December 11 of the same year. The programme allowed applicants to self-certify their eligibility without submitting evidence of pandemic-related business losses. The Federal Bureau of Investigation investigated the case. nigeria.description: Agency intercepts 160 explosives bound for Zamfara, seizes 4.6 tonnes of cannabis in Osun By Kingsley Omonobi The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has arrested a 37-year-old South African professional golfer, Grobler Henlo, and a 25-year-old Kenyan chef, Abubakar Faiza Njambi, over an alleged attempt to smuggle 50.40 kilogrammes of Loud, a potent strain of cannabis, into Nigeria. The suspects were arrested at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA), Ikeja, Lagos, following the interception of the illicit consignment. The NDLEA spokesman, Femi Babafemi, said the golfer’s arrest came exactly one month before the agency intercepted an American professional basketball player, Greene Da’monte Khiree, at the same airport on November 11, 2026, over the importation of 33.95 kilogrammes of the same psychoactive substance. According to the agency, Henlo arrived in Lagos from South Africa aboard a South African Airways flight on October 11 and was intercepted at the Terminal 2 arrival hall. A search of two travelling boxes in his possession reportedly led to the discovery of 46 parcels of Loud weighing 50.40 kilogrammes. Investigations revealed that although the boxes were in Henlo’s possession, they bore the luggage tags of his alleged accomplice, Njambi, who had collected two other boxes bearing his tags from the airport conveyor belt before leaving the airport. The agency said the exchange of luggage tags was a deliberate attempt by the syndicate to frustrate the identification of ownership and enable each courier to deny the boxes bearing their respective names if intercepted. During preliminary questioning, Henlo reportedly disclosed that he was recruited by a South African associate identified as Shanel, who linked him with other members of the syndicate whom he had never met physically. He said a driver picked him up from his home in South Africa, handed him four travelling boxes and took him to the airport, where he was instructed to meet Njambi and exchange luggage tags. The golfer reportedly said he was promised 5,000 South African rand upon successful delivery of the consignment. Further examination revealed that tracking devices had been installed in the travelling boxes and on his mobile phone, a development the agency said was similar to what was discovered in the bags abandoned by the American basketball player a month later. The NDLEA said the discovery showed how closely the cartels monitored their couriers and consignments. It added that the passport biodata page of Njambi, recovered from Henlo’s phone, was used to profile her and place her on the agency’s watchlist. The accident occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, at the river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan communities. The boat was conveying passengers from Ayama to Ukubie community for a burial ceremony when it capsized. NEMA in a statement signed by Manzo Ezeki of NEMA Press Unit, said 24 survivors had been rescued, while 24 bodies had been recovered as of Saturday, bringing the number of confirmed fatalities to 24. Search and rescue operations were still ongoing at the time of the announcement. The agency disclosed that 19 of the survivors were taken to Ayama Clinic, while five others, who sustained varying degrees of injuries, were transferred to Family Care Hospital in Yenagoa for medical treatment. The deployment of the technical team followed the earlier activation of NEMA’s South-South Zonal Directorate and the mobilisation of an emergency response team from its Port Harcourt Operations Office to the accident scene. The agency said it is coordinating the rescue operation alongside the Bayelsa State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA), Nigerian Red Cross Society, Nigeria Police Force, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), local divers and other emergency responders. Governor Douye Diri visited the scene of the accident, where he expressed grief over the loss of lives and condoled with the families of the victims. He also commended the emergency agencies, security operatives, local divers and other responders for their intervention and continued efforts to locate possible survivors despite the difficult riverine terrain. NEMA expressed sympathy with the Bayelsa State Government and the families affected by the tragedy, pledging to sustain its collaboration with relevant authorities to coordinate the rescue operation. entertainment.description: Have you ever spent six hours in an airport waiting for your connecting flight, watching the departure screens, browsing duty-free shops and wondering what the city outside looks like? Perhaps you were connecting through Istanbul, Doha, Dubai or Addis Ababa. You were technically in another country, but the closest you came to experiencing it was buying a souvenir at the airport. What if I told you that some airlines could help you turn that connection into an additional holiday, sometimes even providing accommodation? Having travelled to more than 70 countries, I have learnt that one of the smartest ways to travel is to pay attention to the journey, not just the destination. Many Nigerians book international tickets based on price, travel time and baggage allowance. These are important considerations, but there is another question worth asking: What else can this ticket give me? I am talking about stopovers, not the hurried two-hour connection where you are running between terminals, but an intentional break in your journey that allows you to experience another destination before continuing to the country you originally planned to visit. And with the right airline, itinerary and travel documents, that additional experience might cost less than you imagine. First, Understand What You Are Booking A layover is generally a connection between flights; a stopover is a longer, planned break in your journey. Airlines define these differently, and the distinction matters because some offer special hotel packages, sightseeing tours or complimentary accommodation to qualifying passengers. For example, imagine travelling from Lagos to London through Istanbul. Instead of spending a few hours at Istanbul Airport, you could investigate whether your ticket qualifies for a longer stopover, allowing you to explore Istanbul before continuing to London. You have now turned one international journey into an opportunity to experience two destinations outside Nigeria. The secret is to investigate the stopover before purchasing your ticket, rather than arriving at the airport and hoping the airline will allow you to stay longer. For visa purposes, Nigerians do not qualify, but with a valid Turkish visa you would be able to qualify for some of the perks. entertainment.title: Asali Africa: Serves Up ‘There’s Rice at Home’ A New Cooking Series Hosted by Chef Soliat Bada
entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. Read the full recipe for Rice and Peas with Oxtail . Rice and peas with oxtail, from Episode 1 Soliat Bada and Michael Famoroti in Episode 1 Episode 2 moves to the Gulf for lamb kabsa, Saudi Arabia’s national dish, fragrant with dried lime and seven spice. Soliat is joined by Bella Adeleke , CEO of Asali Africa and founder of the fashion label Garbe, for a conversation about redefining success. Read the full recipe for Lamb Kabsa . entertainment.title: Beyond the Mini LED Label: What Should Define Good Mini LED Performance?
entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? Where TCL Enters The Category Conversation TCL is relevant to that discussion because Mini LED has become a significant part of its global television business. According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. TCL reported 2.43 million Mini LED TV shipments during the period, representing 77.1% year on year growth. That position follows a strong 2025, when TCL reported, based on Omdia data, a 31.1% share of global Mini LED TV shipments and 118.0% year on year shipment growth. Market scale does not, on its own, define technology leadership. What it does provide is evidence that a manufacturer has become an important participant in how the category develops. entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. Before the two teams tangle, we asked columnist Ann Killion and reporters Eric Branch and Harrison Rich for their answers to some key questions about the matchup. Have mounting injuries already ended the prime of Nick Bosa 's career? Is this his new normal in terms of production? Harrison Rich: Bosa has not looked like his old self since returning two weeks ago from a calf injury. He didn't look like himself earlier in the season, either, when he was dealing with knee tendinitis coming off his second torn right ACL. The 29-year-old defensive end hasn't recorded a sack in four games this season, his longest NFL drought. He pointed to two factors Wednesday for his struggles: He's still learning some of the quirks of defensive coordinator Raheem Morris' scheme, and he's still knocking off some rust. Bosa said he took "for granted" some of the things he used to be able to do automatically. Sunday's game, expected to have playoff-like intensity, will tell us a lot about the heights Bosa is still capable of reaching. sports.title: Randy Flores brings a former player's perspective to Houston Astros GM job - and knows its limits
sports.description: From player to scout to Astros GM, Randy Flores says firsthand experience helps him understand players - if he stays open to other perspectives. (Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle) In his first year as St. Louis Cardinals scouting director , Randy Flores was watching a pitcher who threw a four-seam fastball and a curveball. The mix can be the backbone of a north-south pitching profile. But to Flores, a former major-league reliever, it looked suboptimal. "I'm like, ‘No, no, no - you sink it and slide it,'" said Flores, reciting an approach he gleaned from former Cardinals pitching coach Dave Duncan. As a slight left-hander who did not throw especially hard, Flores carved out a playing career that lasted parts of eight major-league seasons. So, his methods had merit. But as an executive now, he recalls the scouting anecdote as something of a cautionary tale. "Being a former player, if you're anchored too much to, ‘This is how it was done when I was playing,' it's the wrong thing," Flores said. Exploring other perspectives and means and finding a balance has been part of Flores' evolution as an executive, one that led to his hiring this month as general manager of the Houston Astros . It is also an arc to which only a handful of the majors' current highest-ranking baseball executives can relate. Of the current presidents of baseball operations, Jerry Dipoto (Mariners), Chris Young (Rangers), Craig Breslow (Red Sox) and Buster Posey (Giants) played in the majors. So did general managers Chris Getz (White Sox) and Flores, whom the Astros hired after 11-plus seasons in St. Louis' front office. That many top executives did not play in the majors, or at all professionally, illustrates how it is far from required. It might even invite the question of how such experience informs former players' approach to the role, if at all, as Flores settles into running a baseball operations department for the first time. "You probably have more empathy … for what a player goes through, from the moment they sign their first professional contract to when they get to the big leagues," Dipoto said at last week's GM meetings in Las Vegas. Dipoto and Breslow were relievers in the majors, like Flores. Dipoto posited that background could help "to understand the life of the guy who (is) not always the most thought-of player on the roster." "Outside of that, I think it's just business as usual," Dipoto said. "We each went through our own, I guess, apprenticeship (after playing). "You take the lessons you learn and apply them, just like any other general manager does when they get their first job. We just maybe have that slight - I don't even want to call it an advantage - that slight difference in that we have lived life in these players' shoes and probably as a result have a little bit more empathy rather than just frustration. sports.description: [BBC] In his latest BBC Sport column, England World Cup winner Matt Dawson reflects on Steve Borthwick's side's record win over New Zealand and previews the final round of Nations Championship fixtures. If England had produced that performance two years ago against New Zealand, there would have been a lap of honour and wild celebrations. Saturday felt like business. Job done, move on. And that is how it should be. It was a record victory for a northern hemisphere side against the All Blacks, yet at full-time you would hardly have known it. Even the post-match messaging from their leaders - Maro Itoje, Ellis Genge and Steve Borthwick - was that this performance had always been in them and that nobody was surprised. However, they will want to back it up. A tired but hurting New Zealand side will arrive at Allianz Stadium next Saturday looking for revenge. England beat the All Blacks in back-to-back Tests in 2002 and 2003. Matching that achievement on Saturday was a significant statement. Three consecutive wins over New Zealand, followed by a third-place finish, would leave England in a strong position heading into 2027, when the Rugby World Cup takes place in Australia. Lose, though, and it will be a waste of some great momentum. We have had many a false dawn with Borthwick's England, but something feels different this time. For me, that comes down to the players taking responsibility. Many of us ex-pros called for it during the Six Nations, and finally we are seeing the players take the lead on the style of rugby they want to play. It is an exciting, free-flowing brand of attacking rugby that mirrors what they are used to playing in the Prem. England's backs can compete with the very best and they tore through New Zealand on multiple occasions. Credit also has to go to Borthwick for allowing the players to take control. That, in itself, shows how he is learning and evolving as a head coach. Once players start getting 40, 50, 60 or 70 caps, they know more about certain aspects of the game than the coach because they are the ones out there experiencing it. If the environment does not allow players to turn around and say 'this isn't going to work', then it is never going to work. The reports before the Australia game suggested honest conversations took place, with the players wanting a greater say in how the team operates. The Six Nations was probably a big turning point. Moura dropped straight to the ground with his hands over his face, covering his head with his jersey as he started crying. He then signalled to the bench that he wanted to be substituted. Moura, who received support from both sets of players following the blunder, was not immediately substituted and later came off in the 70th minute. Empata o USC Paredes numa infelicidade de Francisco Moura 🫨 #sporttvportugal #TAÇAnaSPORTTV #TaçadePortugal #FCPorto #USCParedes pic.twitter.com/KqQQkxEPDq — sport tv (@sporttvportugal) November 20, 2026 The episode prompted a call for support for Moura during Porto's general assembly on Saturday, which drew applause from fellow members. “Members took the opportunity to express their vote of confidence in Francisco Moura,” Porto's general assembly chairman Antonio Tavares said. The cup tie finished 1-1 after extra time, with Porto eventually overcoming Paredes on penalties. Moura had previously faced abuse on social media. He restricted comments on Instagram after conceding a late handball penalty that led to Sporting Lisbon’s equaliser in a league game in February, then temporarily deactivated his account following a draw at Benfica in March.

sports.description: Penn State Wrestling makes their annual trip up the Hudson Valley to West Point for the erstwhile Black Knight Invitational. And, probably more importantly, this event serves as unofficial wrestle offs as the coaches look to set the line up for the season. This year most of the lineup is set with one exception, the matchup to watch is Masanosuke Ono and Nate Desmond at 133 pounds. Coach Cael indicated that Ono won the wrestle off in the practice room but Desmond continues to push and this event should serve as one more data point to determing the starter. sports.title: Manchester City's torrid winless run in the Premier League extended to four games on Saturday afternoon as yet another lacklustre display from Enzo Maresca's men saw the Blues draw 1-1 with Fulham at the Etihad Stadium.
sports.description: Manchester City's torrid winless run in the Premier League extended to four games on Saturday afternoon as yet another lacklustre display from Enzo Maresca's men saw the Blues draw 1-1 with Fulham at the Etihad Stadium. How does Enzo Maresca fix Manchester City's defence? A City performace that was, for large parts, void of intensity and creativity, saw the Blues fail to beat Fulham at the Etihad Stadium for the first time in 15 years, dating back to February 2011 under Roberto Mancini. There was hope that, after the international break, those of a sky-blue persuasion would be galvanised to right the wrongs of their recent shortcomings, having suffered three consecutive league defeats; unfortunately, however, it was more of the slothful same. In the opening exchanges, Maresca's men struggled to ride the storm of Fulham 's intensity but did conjure some somewhat presentable chances early on, with Erling Haaland seeing his effort thwarted by David Affengruber whilst a deflection steered Nico O'Reilly's shot narrowly wide. However, with just 16 minutes on the clock, Manchester City 's defensive frailties reared their ugly head once again as the Cottagers drew first blood in the tie through Rodrigo Muniz, who latched on to a superb pass from former Blue Oscar Bobb and hammered past Gianluigi Donnarumma to give the visitors the lead. Just eight minutes later, the home side thought they had restored parity after an excellent cross from Iliman Ndiaye found Haaland, and the 26-year-old, after squandering the initial chance, seized upon a goalkeeping mishap by Bernd Leno, prodding home after the German appeared to spill the ball. But referee Thomas Bramall, controversially brought the celebrations to an abrupt halt, having adjudged that the former Arsenal shot-stopper had two hands on the ball at the time of the Norwegian's follow-up, resulting in a foul and disallowed goal. Subsequently, a defensive blunder from O'Reilly nearly proved calamitous as the Englishman allowed Bobb to snatch possession inside the Manchester City area, but Donnarumma was on hand to spare his teammate's blushes and deny the Fulham number 14. After a dismal first 45 which saw the halftime whistle met with jeers from the Etihad Stadium crowd, Maresca was in dire need of an injection of impetus into his side, and 12 minutes after the restart, Elliott Anderson obliged, producing a sumptuous volley which nestled into the back of the Fulham net and hauled the hosts level. Whilst the goal certainly did breathe some life into the home side, City were still by no means at their scintillating best in the second period, with the lack of ideas and desire remaining a glaringly obvious issue. In truth, Fulham looked more likely to walk away with three points, but Donnarumma, whose shot-stopping was much improved, remained resolute, preventing both Muniz and Calvin Bassey from deciding the tie late on. sports.title: Coco Gauff Explains Why Dad Corey Was Missing From Her Player Box Despite Family’s Presence at BJK Cup Play-offs
sports.description: Coco Gauff Image via Instagram/@cocogauff Coco Gauff explained her father, Corey Gauff’s, absence from her player box during the Billie Jean King Cup play-offs in her hometown. Following her exit from the WTA Finals, Gauff led Team USA against Hungary in the BJK Cup. She locked horns with Dalma Galfi on Saturday, November 21, 2026, in Delray Beach, Florida. Gauff overwhelmed Galfi from the baseline and saw off her opponent 6-1, 6-1. Gauff was seen being cheered by her mother, Candi, grandmother Yvonne Lee Odom, and her brothers. However, her father was nowhere to be seen in her player’s box. The United States Tennis Association shared a video of her family supporting her and wrote: “Coco Gauff’s family is bringing the hometown support!” The video did not feature her father. Gauff shared the video on her Instagram story and revealed that her father was watching her compete from a different spot around the court. “My dad watches from the back lolll,” Gauff wrote. Screenshot of Coco Gauff’s Instagram story. Coco Gauff’s father was her initial tennis coach. He used to watch his daughter compete from the player’s box. However, in 2023, Corey Gauff decided to move elsewhere in the stadium. Coco Gauff reveals amusing story about her father missing her US Open winning moment After Coco Gauff’s third-round win at the 2026 Australian Open, an interviewer asked Gauff about her father and from where he watches her matches. Gauff revealed that it is always the other people who inform her from where her father is watching her compete. She stated that her father struggles to control his emotions during matches and hence she has asked him not to sit in her player box. “No, it’s other people who tell me (where he is),” she told reporters. “Yeah, the reason why is he can’t control his reactions. It’s not necessarily for me but for him. I told him, ‘We’ve just got to cut it.'” (via Reuters ) Coco Gauff further highlighted the 2023 US Open incident, where she won her first Grand Slam title by seeing off Aryna Sabalenka. The American tennis player’s father was in the stadium gym when she clinched the winning point. An attendant had to inform him of her victory after which he rushed to congratulate her. “I heard when I won the U.S. Open he was in the gym, and the TV was behind so the gym attendant had to tell him I actually won. So he needed to run out and greet me in the crowd. I don’t know where he was at French Open and you probably know more than I do, but yeah, I’ve heard that he’s all around the site, usually like locked in on the screen and just pacing,” Coco Gauff added. Gauff won her second Grand Slam title at the 2025 French Open. sports.title: “Fireable Offense for Matt Campbell”: Brandon Walker Blasts Penn State HC After Meltdown vs. Rutgers
sports.description: Matt Campbell During a Press Conference © Imagn Penn State head coach Matt Campbell was put on the hot seat by Barstool Sports’ Brandon Walker following the Nittany Lions’ 25-24 loss to Rutgers on Saturday. The Nittany Lions entered the matchup as clear favorites against a Rutgers team that had won just two games all season. However, the Scarlet Knights ultimately blew Penn State’s two-score lead. After the game, Walker called out Campbell for the loss against Rutgers, deeming it a fireable offense. “I honestly think that might be a fireable offense for Matt Campbell at Penn State. You can’t ever lose to Rutgers,” Walker wrote on X. Penn State had led 16-0 and later held a 24-10 advantage with less than 11 minutes remaining. Rutgers pulled off a stunning comeback. Rutgers running back Antwan Raymond caught a pass short of the goal line and lateraled to wide receiver Ben Black III, who scored on the final play of regulation. Rutgers converted the ensuing two-point attempt to take a 25-24 lead. Time ran out before Penn State could reply. The loss against Rutgers was particularly damaging because it ended Penn State’s 18-game winning streak against the Scarlet Knights. Penn State last lost in 1988. HC Matt Campbell Takes Responsibility for Penn State’s Collapse In his post-game conference, Penn State head coach Matt Campbell took responsibility for the loss to Rutgers. “I didn’t have us prepared to play our best football game, Senior Day, the end of the season, and that really hurts me, and it puts a lot of responsibility on my shoulders,” Campbell said via Go PSU Sports. “To me, our ability to do hard things is still keeping this team from becoming its best.” Campbell added that the team has failed to be excellent for the full 60 minutes, leading to poor finishes in several games. Previously, the Nittany Lions failed to close the game against Wisconsin. On Saturday, they allowed Rutgers 15 unanswered points. Penn State quarterback Rocco Becht and running back Cam Wallace committed two costly fumbles in the loss. As a result, the Nittany Lions could only manage 26 yards of offense in the fourth quarter. Penn State entered the matchup against Rutgers after recording three straight wins. They had the momentum and were making progress under Campbell before the latest heartbreaking loss. Penn State fell to 6-5 overall and 3-5 in Big Ten play. The Nittany Lions will conclude their regular season against Maryland on November 28. sports.title: Mikel Arteta confirms major Arsenal injury blow after Newcastle United clash
sports.description: Mikel Arteta confirms major Arsenal injury blow after Newcastle United clash David Raya Injury Concern Clouds Arsenal After Newcastle Draw Arsenal left St James’ Park with a point, but the bigger issue is in goal. David Raya, one of the key reasons behind Arsenal’s strong opening to the season, went off injured in the 2-2 draw with Newcastle and now faces scans on a suspected shoulder problem. The sequence was straightforward enough. Raya collided with William Osula while trying to release the ball, went down in clear discomfort and needed treatment on the pitch. He could not continue. He walked off, headed straight down the tunnel and that will worry Arsenal far more than the dropped points. There is no need to dress it up. If Raya is out, it is a problem. He has been reliable, calm and productive, with seven clean sheets in Arsenal’s first ten Premier League games. That sort of consistency matters, particularly for a side heading into a run that can shape its season. Photo IMAGO Mikel Arteta Awaits David Raya Scan Results Mikel Arteta offered no certainty after the match, saying: “Unfortunately, he had to come off, which is not good news. “He will have an MRI assessment tomorrow, but at the moment I don’t know.” He added: “It was a knock, I don’t know how it happened and what the injury is at the moment. We have to wait and see tomorrow. “We know how important David is for us. Tomorrow we will have more news.” Arsenal Fixtures Make Raya Injury More Serious Kepa Arrizabalaga replaced Raya for the final 20 minutes, entering with Arsenal 2-1 down. By full-time it had finished 2-2, though the result quickly became secondary. Arsenal had led at the break through Eberechi Eze, then lost control after half-time as Newcastle turned the game. Now comes the difficult part. Arsenal host Manchester City next weekend, with Real Madrid, Tottenham and Manchester United also on the schedule before Christmas. If Raya misses any part of that spell, Arsenal’s margin for error shrinks. There is enough quality in the squad, but goalkeeper injuries are different. You do not rotate calm, command and trust so easily.

sports.title: Watford sack boss Dionisi after 18 games
sports.description: Alessio Dionisi was the fifth Italian manager hired by Watford under the ownership of the Pozzo family [Getty Images] Watford are looking for their sixth manager in 18 months after they sacked head coach Alessio Dionisi following 18 games in charge. The 46-year-old Italian was appointed in June after the departure of Ed Still, who himself lasted only three months at Vicarage Road. Still, Javi Gracia and Paulo Pezzolano were all also given full-time contracts after Tom Cleverley left in May 2025. Dionisi was Watford's 12th head coach, not including interim bosses, since the end of the 2020-21 season, and leaves the Hornets searching for a 25th since the Pozzo family took over the club in 2012. The club have had 57 permanent managers in their 145-year history. The decision to replace him comes after Saturday's crushing 4-0 defeat by Sheffield United at Bramall Lane. Dionisi's dismissal caps an underwhelming start to the season, with the Hornets having won just four league games to leave them 21st in the table. "We thank Alessio and his staff for his professionalism and their efforts," sporting director Luke Dowling told the club website. "As I'm sure the supporters have seen, Alessio is a really good guy and we wish him the best for the future. "The process has started for a replacement and we hope to be in a position to announce that shortly." Dionisi was sacked by Serie B club Empoli in March after only five months in charge following a run of five wins in 22 matches. His spell in charge of the Hornets was his first outside his homeland and started promisingly when his youthful side beat Southampton in their opening league game. But they won only two of their next 12 in all competitions, and despite deservedly beating Charlton on 17 October, reverses at Wolves and Norwich followed, before four points from Dionisi's final three games in charge of the Hertfordshire side and his dismissal means further upheaval for the Hornets. With more than a third of the league season complete, Watford are one place outside of the Championship relegation zone (table shown before Burnley face Blackburn on Sunday) [BBC] Since sacking Cleverley at the end of the 2024-25 campaign, the club has now been through four permanent head coaches, as well as interim boss Charlie Daniels' two-game spell in charge. Of those four, only Gracia, in his second spell at Vicarage Road, took charge of more than 20 games. On the morning of their final-day drubbing by Coventry last season, chief executive Scott Duxbury wrote a statement on the club website saying Watford had made mistakes, labelling their end to the campaign "unacceptable" and "truly disappointing in the extreme". sports.title: 'I fulfilled a dream!' - Leandro Paredes reacts to winning silverware as Juan Roman Riquelme lands first title as Boca Juniors president
sports.description: Atletico Mineiro v Boca Juniors - Copa CONMEBOL Sudamericana 2026 Final - Getty Images Sport Leandro Paredes celebrated a dream fulfilled as Boca Juniors beat Atletico Mineiro 2-0 to win a record third Copa Sudamericana title and hand Juan Roman Riquelme his first international trophy as president. Their triumph in Barranquilla ended an 18-year continental wait for the club. Paredes celebrates as Riquelme claims first title Boca Juniors defeated Atletico Mineiro 2-0 at the Estadio Metropolitano Roberto Melendez in Barranquilla to become the first three-time Copa Sudamericana champions. Santiago Ascacibar opened the scoring in the 16th minute before Miguel Merentiel struck three minutes into the second half. The victory ended Boca's 18-year wait for an international trophy since the 2008 Recopa and gave club president Juan Roman Riquelme his first continental crown as an executive. Having won three Copa Libertadores titles in Boca's number 10 shirt as a player, Riquelme now shares continental silverware with the Xeneize from the directors' box. Paredes hails dream title after returning home Leandro Paredes captained and drove Boca's campaign after returning to the club, leading CONMEBOL competitions in 2026 with 791 completed passes, 234 final-third passes and 212 line-breaking passes. Speaking to ESPN after the final whistle, Paredes shared his emotion at winning silverware back in Azul y Oro . "I fulfilled a dream," Paredes said. "I always dreamed of being able to win a title. I only have words of gratitude for the club. Thanks to my children, my family and my friends. Since I was little, I've been taught to compete and win everything possible. I love winning and competing. I'm lucky to achieve important things." Riquelme's mid-year reset and Villa's impact After finishing third in Copa Libertadores Group D, Boca pivoted in June under Riquelme's leadership by appointing former team-mate Rodolfo Arruabarrena as head coach and bringing in players including Sebastian Villa, who assisted Merentiel's second-half goal in Barranquilla. Back in March at the CONMEBOL group draw, Riquelme had already spoken of the pull of continental football , saying: "Playing in the Copa always creates excitement, both in the squad and among our fans." Villa also highlighted his joy after helping Boca past O'Higgins, Deportivo Recoleta, Sao Paulo and Vasco da Gama on the way to the final. "I'm very happy, thank God it happened, returning to the club that gave me the opportunity," Villa told ESPN. "I came back with great enthusiasm and a desire for a title. I've won two in a row." Libertadores return and Recopa await in 2027 Lifting the Copa Sudamericana brings a USD 10,000,000 champions' prize and direct entry into the 2027 Copa Libertadores group stage without qualifying rounds. sports.title: Gameday column: Bills and the current state of strength of schedule
sports.description: It’s like each week there’s arisen a new narrative about this Buffalo Bills team. Leading into Week 11 against the Dolphins, it was all about strength of schedule… probably because of Buffalo’s competition — or lack thereof — since the bye week. I’ll be the first to mention that teams are not always what their record says they are. But what these Bills are doing is subtly different from previous Bills teams during the Josh Allen era. What has remained the same is Buffalo’s regular-season dominance. Since 2020, the Bills have been the NFL’s best team in the regular season. They have the most wins and the highest point differential by an insane margin. But like I wrote a week ago, the Sean McDermott clubs always had an uncharacteristic stumble or two during said regular season that kept them away out of the No. 1 seat in the AFC playoffs. Of course today, against the Dolphins, represents one of those “stumble” possibilities with the colossal clash on Thanksgiving against the Chiefs looming. But that’s the not the crux of this column. Are the Bills the best 8-1 team in NFL history? No. Are they the best 8-1 team in the past decade. No. But they’ve done exactly what a team should do against the competition level it has faced. Regarding the aforementioned point differential, it’s my absolute favorite measure of team quality… because it’s straightforward and pretty darn predictive. How’s this for point differential’s stickiness — 11 of the past 12 Super Bowl winners finished the regular season in the Top 6 in point differential. Insane, right? From 2004 – 2025, 17 of 22 of the clubs that hoisted the Lombardi Trophy at season’s end were a Top 6 point-differential team during the regular season. And this Bills team enters this AFC East game against the Dolphins second in point differential, at +88. If Buffalo had been squeaking by lesser opponents regularly, I’d be the first to write their 8-1 feels phony. That hasn’t been the case whatsoever. And teams can only play the opponents on their schedule. Among the nine teams at 7-2 or better right now, only the Broncos (.583) and Vikings (.518) have faced a cumulative opponent win percentage above .500. The Bills are third on that list at .480, as their opponents have a combined record of 40-47. The combined record of Chiefs’ opponents to date is 34-53 (.391). They’re currently in last in that metric. (another shoutout to Jeremy White from WGR550 who noticed this earlier this week.) Oh, and as for the strength-of-schedule element that legitimately matters come playoff-seeding time — the Bills currently have the second-best strength of victory at .455, behind only the Broncos, the sole AFC club with a strength of victory over .500. On this note, the first half of the 2026 NFL season has shown a more sizable gap between the great teams and the noticeably bad ones. science.title: 10 things that worry me about chasing the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt
science.description: null On Aug. 2, 2027, I'll be in Luxor, Egypt, to witness what could be the greatest total solar eclipse of my life. I've seen nine total solar eclipses across the world, but this one promises to be different. For a remarkable six minutes and 22 seconds, the moon will completely cover the sun, plunging Egypt's ancient temples and monuments into eerie twilight as the solar corona bursts into view. I've been calling it the "eclipse of the century" for many years, and for good reason. It will be the longest total solar eclipse until 2114 — and the longest on land of the 21st century — and it will take place in one of the most extraordinary places on Earth. What could go wrong? I've chased eclipses long enough to know that the celestial mechanics are the easy part. The moon will arrive exactly on schedule — that's guaranteed. Everything else — the weather, the crowds, the transport, the equipment and the people — is rather less predictable. From the possibility of dust storms to uncertainty about whether boats will even be allowed to move on the Nile, there are plenty of reasons to be slightly wary about what awaits eclipse chasers after the ultimate bragging rights on Aug. 2, 2027. Here are the 10 things worrying me most about the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt. A dust storm could make the eclipsed sun less impressive. (Image credit: Grant Faint via Getty Images) 1. A sudden dust storm The chances of cloud-free skies in Luxor and anywhere in Upper Egypt in August are exceptionally high — close to 100%. That's almost unheard of in eclipse-chasing. However, clouds aren't the only thing that can obscure the sun. Dust and sand are potential hazards in the Egyptian desert, and a dust storm at the wrong moment could affect—though probably not ruin—the view. Although the sun will almost certainly be visible during the eclipse, airborne dust could hide the delicate structure of the solar corona. 2. Chaos in Luxor How many people will descend on Luxor for the eclipse? August is normally a quiet month for tourism in Luxor because of the oppressive heat. In 2027, however, the city and its surrounding urban area — population about four million — could swell as eclipse chasers, tour groups, photographers and curious visitors descend. Hotels, roads, buses and archaeological sites will all face extraordinary pressure. My biggest concern isn't necessarily the number of people watching the eclipse, but the logistical chaos it will create. Let's take Mallorca as an example for the 2026 eclipse. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
science.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."

Following the sad news of Sir Patrick Stewart's passing , there's been no shortage of discussion about his best moments as Captain Jean-Luc Picard . "The Inner Light"'s life in 25 minutes is a strong contender, as are the courtroom grandstanding in "The Measure of a Man" and his insistence (under extreme torture) that "there are four lights!" in "Chain of Command". But for this writer's money, it's hard to look past a nine-minute sequence in "Star Trek: First Contact", which turns 30 this weekend. With the Borg overrunning the newly launched USS Enterprise-E, Picard — who has long-standing beef with the Collective, following his assimilation in classic "The Next Generation" story " The Best of Both Worlds " — orders his crew to fight the cybernetic nasties hand-to-hand if required, defying their pleas to activate the ship's self-destruct system and retreat. He even calls Worf — not a man renowned for dodging a fight — a coward, prompting the Klingon to respond that, "If you were any other man, I would kill you where you stand." Ouch. science.title: SpaceX will retire 1st Starship upper stage ever caught by 'chopsticks,' Elon Musk says
science.description: null The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit . He didn't say where Ship would be put on display, but the likeliest locale is Starbase, SpaceX's Starship manufacturing and launch hub. (SpaceX plans to shift most Starship launches to its new Starbase Louisiana site, but construction has yet to begin on that $100 billion complex.) Musk participated virtually in the TomorrowX conversation, which was moderated by two friends of his, the venture capitalists Gavin Baker and Antonio Gracias. (TomorrowX took place in Austin, Texas, but Musk was in China on Wednesday as part of President Trump's delegation for his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.) The world's richest man expounded on Ship 42's historic achievement, explaining that it gets SpaceX much closer to the "holy grail of rocketry" — a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. Before Flight 15, SpaceX had already caught Starship's first-stage booster, known as Super Heavy, on three separate occasions , and it had reflown a booster twice. But the company had never attempted a Ship catch, which is a taller order, given how much faster and farther Starship upper stages fly. So snagging Ship on the first try was a very big deal, according to Musk. "Everyone knew, within SpaceX, at least, how important this milestone was, and that it was really something fundamental and profound — that Starship will be the first-ever fully reusable orbital space system," he told Baker and Gracias on Wednesday. The Ship upper stage of SpaceX's Starship megarocket comes back to its launch tower for a "chopsticks" catch on Nov. 14, 2026, during the vehicle's 15th test flight. science.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo probe arrives in orbit around Mercury today
science.description: null Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. The big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio. The duo launched — along with a power and propulsion element called the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) — aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana in October 2018 , beginning a long and looping trip through the inner solar system. Mercury is a difficult planet to reach because it's so close to the sun . Spacecraft approaching the solar system's innermost planet are accelerated to high velocities by the immense gravitational pull of our star and must shed a great deal of kinetic energy to be captured by Mercury's much weaker tug. So the BepiColombo team designed a trajectory that featured one flyby of Earth , two of Venus and six of Mercury over the course of about seven years. That flight time was increased by a year , however, after the mission suffered an issue with its solar panels, which reduced the power available for the MTM's electric thrusters. BepiColombo's arrival at Mercury will take a total of about six months. (Image credit: European Space Agency) Today's orbital insertion is the latest milestone in BepiColombo's Mercury arrival phase, which is expected to take about six months in total. Arrival began on Sept. 3, when the MTM released MPO and Mio. The two orbiters remain connected today; they won't separate until Dec. 9 or thereabouts. Shortly thereafter, Mio will settle into its final orbit, a highly elliptical path that will take it over Mercury's poles. MPO is also destined for a polar orbit, though a much less elliptical one than Mio's; the ESA probe will conduct a series of engine burns before finally getting there on March 10, 2027. BepiColombo won't start doing science work until April 6, 2027. The two probes will gather complementary data from their two different vantage points, shedding a great deal of light on a mysterious world. "The mission will study all aspects of Mercury, from the structure and dynamics of its magnetosphere and how it interacts with the solar wind , to its internal structure with its large iron core, and the origin of the planet’s magnetic field," ESA officials wrote in a BepiColombo mission description . "The data will enable scientists to understand more about the origin and evolution of a planet located close to its parent star, and a better understanding of the overall evolution of our solar system," they added.

The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth about 8.5 minutes later, touching down in the Pacific Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You."
